customManagers.description: Swift releases. swiftlang/swift tags them swift-X.Y.Z-RELEASE. Version and commit are captured by ONE regex so Renovate moves them together -- verify-relocatable.sh asserts the clone of SWIFT_TAG is exactly SWIFT_SHA, so a version bumped without its commit fails closed.

The swiftlang/llvm-project commit the build support is cut from. llvm-project tags every Swift release swift-X.Y.Z-RELEASE, exactly as swiftlang/swift does, so this tracks that tag the same way the Swift pin is tracked: version and commit in ONE regex, moved together. The version is LLVM_SWIFT_RELEASE rather than SWIFT_VERSION only because two managers capturing the same literal would both rewrite it; build-llvm.sh fails unless the two are equal and LLVM_SHA is the commit at the tag. This replaced a git-refs manager on a branch pin, which Renovate could only move within one branch -- never to the next release's.

packageRules.description: ONE PR per Swift release, moving the Swift pin and the llvm-project pin together. Apart, each PR fails build-llvm.sh's check that both name the same release, so neither could ever merge. Together they build and ship -- patch, minor or major, the family default -- because the one thing a green build used to miss here, Swift built against another release's LLVM, now fails the build instead of passing it.
